Please read /papers/investigations-5/07_positive_theta_primitives/01_jensen/01_mellin_curvature/notes/05_CONTINUATION_PARALLEL_PHYSICAL_DIRECTIONS_20261101.md. Execute this parallel assessment packet for all six physical directions. Follow the six local overviews and canonical progress files, use disjoint worker ownership within the available concurrency, retain the complete signed theta observable, and give each branch one bounded assessment followed by separate checking. Save the returns, reviews and coordinator synthesis, and report which new input, if any,  advances the Mellin comparison. Return scoped failures honestly and do not start unspecified numerical campaigns.

Part of the goal is also to find an interesting reformulation of RH as a physical theory. It would be especially interesting to use some of the advanced tools within theoretical physics to help with the problems we are facing here. So even if it is not possible to make direct progress, a useful, nontrivial or new reformulation could be interesting in its own right.

I’ll read the assessment packet and repository guidance, then assign disjoint branches within the available concurrency. I’ll assess both possible advances to the Mellin comparison and useful physical reformulations, and have each return checked separately.

All six branch registers are unstarted. I’ve confirmed this session is Astra at ultra effort and registered the chat in the Mellin investigation. I’ll use two waves of three workers; each will select one bounded candidate and return either a derivation, a precise missing estimate, or a scoped failure. Physical reformulations will be assessed on their own merits as well as for any quantitative gain.

The main difficulty is now fixed across the assignments: a positive carrier measure does not make the theta insertion positive. The first wave is examining the source’s thermal identities, the full signed saddle expansion, and an inserted Ward identity. Each must retain the negative region and identify what remains unbounded.

The first wave has identified concrete obligations. The thermal route exposes a failure of positivity-only reasoning, and the Ward route retains an explicit mixed response term. The Mellin route has derived a normalized susceptibility formulation with a nonzero saddle prefactor; it still needs bounds on the complete integrals outside the saddle region. These findings are provisional until checked.

The thermal and Ward returns are being finalized. The Mellin formulation has a potentially useful feature: it expresses the target through signed normalized moments, so a proof need not differentiate an uncontrolled asymptotic error. The next wave will test orbital operators, coefficient deformations, and a concrete protected-observable candidate.

The first three returns are saved, and the second wave is underway. None has yet proved a new Mellin inequality. The main reusable results so far are a complete thermal-observable formula, an exact inserted Ward identity with a stated nonclosure, and a local three-particle Gaussian limit with explicit remaining integral bounds.

Two substantive physical reformulations are emerging from the second wave. One represents all coefficient minors as fermionic transfer amplitudes, with a concrete obstruction to treating that transfer as an equilibrium operator. The other puts the theta function into a normalizable quantum-oscillator state, where RH becomes an alignment condition on its phase-space zeros. Both need separate checking and remain distinct from a sign estimate.

The fermionic branch is saved: it gives an exact all-minor RH reformulation and shows why ordinary self-adjoint transfer-operator positivity cannot settle this particular model. The oscillator and supersymmetric returns are finishing. I’m starting the separate Sol checks against frozen files; any defects will be recorded in reviews or addenda, preserving the original returns.

All six assessments are saved. The separate reviewers have found no mathematical defect so far in the thermal and fermionic returns. They are now checking the local Gaussian limit, oscillator-state construction, inserted Ward identity, and supersymmetric obstruction—especially the distinction between exact reformulations and estimates that remain unproved.

The separate checks accept the oscillator reformulation and the local Gaussian reduction at their stated scopes. The supersymmetric review adds a precise operator-domain clarification; its main conclusion is unchanged. I’m consolidating the results around two outcomes: useful physical formulations are now explicit, while the complete signed Mellin bound still needs a new estimate.

All six assessments and their separate reviews are saved. None proves a new range of the Mellin comparison. The strongest analytical lead is the signed saddle-localization problem; the clearest physical reformulation is an explicit oscillator state whose Husimi zeros encode RH. I’m checking the saved record and links now. No numerical campaign was started.

The final checks passed: all six returns and six reviews match their frozen versions, and all 1,194 local links checked resolve. The synthesis and completion record are saved. I’m refreshing the research chat archive before the final report.

Completed all six bounded assessments and separate cross-model reviews. Saved the [coordinator synthesis](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/07_positive_theta_primitives/01_jensen/01_mellin_curvature/notes/06_PARALLEL_PHYSICAL_DIRECTIONS_SYNTHESIS_20261101.md) and [assessment linking all returns and reviews](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/07_positive_theta_primitives/01_jensen/01_mellin_curvature/reviews/01_PARALLEL_PHYSICAL_DIRECTIONS_ASSESSMENT_20261101.md).

**No branch proves a new range of the Mellin comparison.** The complete signed theta observable was retained throughout.

| Direction | Checked outcome |
|---|---|
| Circle thermal trace | Exact thermal representation; positivity alone leaves the signed response uncontrolled. |
| Fermionic correlators | Bounded fermionic transfer with an all-sector positivity condition equivalent to RH; a scoped obstruction to making this transfer self-adjoint. |
| Connected Mellin response | Resolved saddle cancellation, local Gaussian limit, and explicit sufficient localization bounds. The full signed integrals remain uncontrolled. |
| Biorthogonal ensembles | Exact inserted Ward identity; the selected finite-polynomial closure fails. |
| Schur/Toda structure | Exact source-heat evolution, finite-prefix nonclosure, and a normalizable quantum oscillator formulation. |
| Supersymmetric theory | Exact circle-theory response; the required observable is unprotected. The selected protected class erases the needed spectrum. |

**The most interesting physical outcome is the oscillator formulation:** an explicit normalizable state has Bargmann function proportional to \(\xi((1+z)/2)\). RH is equivalent to all zeros of its Husimi coherent-state probability lying on the imaginary quadrature axis. Physical preparation and a useful dynamical inequality remain open; no novelty claim is made.

The strongest analytical next step is **MC03-B02**: prove the complete signed localization bounds with an explicit threshold, or identify precisely which bound fails. A deferred physical alternative assesses one operational realization of the oscillator evolution.

These next tasks remain unstarted. No numerical campaign ran. All six return/review pairs passed integrity checks, and the saved navigation has no missing file targets.
